dedupe_keys.name: renton washington nine proposed detention ponds under climate change pcswmm stormwater study

description: This case study is a Scientific Reports paper that tests how nine proposed detention ponds across the city of Renton, Washington, would perform under climate change. The authors first build a statistical model of stormwater pollutant loads for the present and future periods, then calibrate an urban drainage model in the PCSWMM platform to quantify runoff and pollutant loads, and run 100-year design storms for future climate scenarios. Loads of stormwater pollutants rise significantly from 2023 to 2050 compared with the 2000 to 2014 record. The ponds are likely to reduce ammonia by 18 to 86 percent, nitrite by 35 to 70, nitrate by 36 to 65, total phosphate by 26 to 91 and suspended solids by 34 to 81 percent, and performance varies with size and location. Coverage: one city, nine ponds, with a calibrated and validated watershed model; peak flow reduction is also discussed. Access: free journal article; the article is CC BY 4.0, and the model files were not looked for. Caveats: ponds are proposed, not built, and results rest on one calibrated watershed and the chosen climate scenarios. It supports climate-adaptive stormwater design and capacity planning studies, and relates to the EPA National Stormwater Calculator record in the catalogue.
